subject: ClinicalAI: request for EU-only model binding and no-fallback during pilot
messages:
From: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@clinicalai.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: alex.rivera@clinicalai.com, legal@clinicalai.com
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 14:15:00 +0000
Subject: Pilot ask: EU-only serving + no-fallback requirement

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. We're preparing to run a small clinical summarization pilot with EU patient data and have a hard constraint from our compliance team: during the pilot we need (a) model inference pinned to an EU region only and (b) a no-fallback policy — we cannot have requests routed to non-EU variants or public hosted models even as a temporary fallback.

Can Redwood support this in a pilot contract? If not feasible, please outline what mitigations you can offer (e.g., guaranteed pin with documented fail-safes, ops runbooks, or a contract clause). We are working to finalize the SOW and need to know by Wednesday.

Attachments: ClinicalAI_DataResidency_Specs.pdf

Best,
Emma Taylor
Head of Partnerships, ClinicalAI

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@clinicalai.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: EU-only serving + no-fallback requirement

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and the spec. Looping in Product (Markus), Security (Irene) and Ops (Connor) to confirm feasibility and the exact contract language.

High-level: Redwood supports region pinning and private deployments, but the strict no-fallback constraint is operationally sensitive — it affects our ability to preserve availability under infra failures. We should be able to put together a pilot plan that meets ClinicalAI's compliance needs with a few tradeoffs (e.g., scheduled maintenance windows, SLA carveouts, on-call escalation paths).

I'll aim to get a short technical + contractual proposal by end of day Tuesday.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:07:00 +01:00
Subject: RE: Pilot ask: EU-only serving + no-fallback requirement

On Mon, 16 Feb 2026 at 10:02 -05:00, hannah_schmitt wrote:
> Emma — thanks for the clear ask and the spec. Looping in Product (Markus), Security (Irene) and Ops (Connor) to confirm feasibility and the exact contract language.

Short answer from Product: we can implement a strict region-tethered policy for the pilot by provisioning a dedicated EU-only serving pool (Dedicated or Private) and enforcing a routing policy that returns a 503 rather than falling back. That satisfies the 'no fallback' semantics but has availability implications — a transient failure in that pool will mean traffic is rejected until we fix capacity or the customer accepts manual failover.

Options to offer ClinicalAI:
- Dedicated EU pool with capacity commit + explicit SLA carveout for regional outages (recommended for highest assurances).
- Private deployment (VPC) hosted in their EU tenant — highest control but longer lead time and higher cost.
- Canary plan: start with EU-only but include an emergency runbook that requires a signed on-call approval to enable limited fallback in a declared incident.

We should include concrete acceptance criteria for the pilot (max allowed downtime, maintenance windows, capacity buffer). Connor — can you confirm ops runbook and how quickly we could spin a dedicated EU pool?

— Markus

From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 14:23:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Pilot ask: EU-only serving + no-fallback requirement

Markus / Hannah — ops feasibility note:

We can provision a dedicated EU-only pool on GCP (Frankfurt) within 7 business days if we prioritize the request. For a pilot with production-like load (we estimate 10k req/day), we'd require at least 2-3 instances (N+1) to avoid immediate capacity loss on a single VM failure.

Behavior for no-fallback: current router can be configured to enforce region binding and return 503 on incompatible variants. However, two things to raise:
1) Automatic scaling lag — if traffic spikes faster than autoscaler can add capacity, some requests will be rejected (503).
2) Zonal infra failures — if the pool becomes unreachable, there is no silent fallback — the client will see errors until we either failover manually or spin up new capacity in-region.

We can mitigate with: warm standby nodes (adds cost), scheduled maintenance windows, and an ops-runbook that includes a manual failover approval flow. I'll attach a short runbook draft and a cost delta for warm standby.

Attachment: SOW_ClinicalAI_Q1_v2.docx

— Connor
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, legal@clinicalai.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 13:02:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Pilot ask: Pilot contract language and security sign-off

Hi team — security sign-off summary for the proposal:

- Data residency: OK if all inference endpoints and logs are kept in the EU region and KMS keys remain in-customer EU KMS. ClinicalAI's spec is compatible with our Private or Dedicated model.
- No-fallback: we can document "no-fallback" as a contractual requirement that Redwood will enforce via routing policies; we should add a clause that defines allowed outage behaviour (e.g., Redwood will not perform automatic cross-region fallback but will maintain manual escalation procedures).
- Acceptance criteria: require a capacity test (pre-launch load test) and a runbook walkthrough with ClinicalAI ops. We should also require a signed change process to enable fallback — this protects both parties.

Next steps I propose:
1) Hannah to send ClinicalAI a short one-page pilot SOW that includes: chosen deployment mode (Dedicated EU), capacity commit, SLA carveouts, on-call escalation flow and the clause that fallback requires mutual written approval.
2) Ops to provide a cost delta for warm standby and a schedule for provisioning.
3) Legal to review tightened language (Laura to lead).

If everyone agrees, I'll prepare the security appendix language.

— Irene Choi
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
